Until you make the unconscious conscious, it will direct your life and you will call it fate.
（除非你将潜意识转化为意识，否则它将主宰你的人生，而你却称之为命运。）
Carl Jung

Attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity.
（注意力是慷慨最罕见、最纯粹的形式。）
Simone Weil

Life can only be understood backwards; but it must be lived forwards.
(生活只能向后理解，但必须向前生活。)
Søren Kierkegaard

You must be ready to burn yourself in your own fire: how could you become new if you have not first become ashes?
(你必须准备好在自己的烈焰中燃烧自己：若不先化为灰烬，你怎能渴望新生？)
Friedrich Nietzsche

To try always to conquer myself rather than fortune, and to alter my desires rather than the order of the world.
(永远致力于征服自己而非命运，去改变自身的欲望而非世界的秩序。)
René Descartes

Hope is not the conviction that something will turn out well, but the certainty that something makes sense, regardless of how it turns out.
(希望并非笃定某事终将圆满，而是确信某事定有意义，无论其结局如何。)
Vaclav Havel

The value of things is not the time they last, but the intensity with which they occur. That is why there are unforgettable moments, inexplicable things and incomparable people.
(事物的价值不在于其持续的时间，而在于其发生时的强烈程度。正因如此，才有了难忘的瞬间、不可名状的事物与无可比拟的人。)
Fernando Pessoa

Perhaps everything terrible is in its deepest being something helpless that wants help from us.
(或许一切可怕的事物，在其最深处都是某种无助的存在，正渴求着我们的救助。)
Rainer Maria Rilke

Time is a river which sweeps me along, but I am the river; it is a tiger which destroys me, but I am the tiger; it is a fire which consumes me, but I am the fire.
(时间是一条将我卷走其中的河流，但我即是河流；它是一只摧毁我的猛虎，但我即是猛虎；它是一场吞噬我的大火，但我即是大火。)
Jorge Luis Borges

Sometimes, just knowing that there are endless fresh things for me to enjoy is enough to make me glad to be alive.
(有时候，仅仅是知道世间还有无尽的新鲜事物供我欣赏，就足以让我觉得活着真好。)
— Etty Hillesum

Love is the extremely difficult realization that something other than oneself is real.
(爱是一种极其艰难的领悟：认识到除自己之外的事物同样是真实存在的。)
Iris Murdoch
